name: TN-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+13 district with an open Republican-held seat
Garrett's lopsided money edge: roughly $2.4M raised versus about $35K for Croley
Prediction markets price a Republican hold near 95 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; Democratic campaign shows minimal infrastructure
model.rationale: The district's thirteen-point Republican lean, Garrett's roughly seventy-to-one fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 95 percent for the GOP all point the same direction. With no polls or expert ratings flagging competition and the Democrat showing almost no financial footprint, the open seat stays firmly in Republican hands.
model.watch: A Garrett scandal, a late surge of Democratic outside spending, or a landslide-scale national environment shift would be needed to put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John Rose (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
John Rose's retirement to run for governor leaves this Republican-leaning Tennessee district open, and the GOP enters as a heavy favorite. The seat carries a roughly thirteen-point Republican partisan lean, and Johnny Garrett has raised about $2.4 million with more than $600,000 in outside support, while Democrat Mike Croley has raised about $35,000 and reports only a few thousand dollars on hand.

Prediction markets give Republicans about a 95 percent chance of holding the seat, and no public polls or expert ratings flag any competitive threat. Two independents are on the ballot but show no fundraising activity. Barring a major scandal or a historic shift in the national environment, the Republican is positioned to hold the seat comfortably in November.
